description: Behaviour lives here in Git (single source of truth). The Mend app is only the runner — nothing app-specific lives at Mend (all images/charts/k0s are public, no registry creds).

kubernetes.description: Renovate's kubernetes manager has no default file scope — point it at our manifests so image tags (e.g. viren070/aiostreams) get bump PRs.

flux.description: Our HelmReleases + HelmRepositories live under infrastructure/ and observability/, not the flux manager's default flux/ dir — point it here so pinned chart versions (cilium, traefik, cert-manager, loki, kube-prometheus-stack…) get bump PRs. Config-only: nothing deploys until a PR is merged and Flux reconciles it.

customManagers.description: k0s host binary pinned in bootstrap.sh — PR on new releases; apply stays deliberate (Autopilot Plan, ADR 0015). Tags look like v1.35.2+k0s.0.

Flux CLI pinned in bootstrap.sh. Same depName as the controllers in gotk-components.yaml (flux manager), so both land in one branch and the CLI never lags the cluster. Neither is applied by a reconcile: clusters/bretagne/flux-system is outside the sync path, apply it with `kubectl apply -k`.

Cilium chart version of the pre-Flux helm install in bootstrap.sh (Flux needs a CNI before it can run). Same depName and registry as the HelmRelease, so a rebuilt node starts on the version Flux will keep.

gVisor (runsc) host binary pinned in bootstrap.sh — PR on new releases; apply stays deliberate and supervised (ADR 0027 §6, same host-substrate flow as K0S_VERSION). google/gvisor has no published GitHub Releases, only tags (release-20260622.0 style), so this uses github-tags, not github-releases.
Helm CLI pinned in bootstrap.sh (pre-Flux Cilium install, operator use; Flux's helm-controller carries its own Helm).
SOPS CLI pinned in bootstrap.sh (decrypts the repository's age-encrypted secrets at bootstrap).
Kata Containers static release pinned in bootstrap.sh. KATA_SHA256 pins the amd64 asset and Renovate cannot compute it: a Kata PR is complete only once KATA_SHA256 is updated in the same branch.
ttyd behind terminal.bretagne.dev, pinned in bootstrap.sh and as provision.sh's default. Restarting ttyd-terminal.service kills every process started from the web terminal (KillMode=control-group).
oauth2-proxy in front of terminal.bretagne.dev (host service, not the in-cluster image), pinned in bootstrap.sh and as provision.sh's default.

packageRules.description: k0s updates are NOT applied by Flux — the PR is a trigger, you apply the update deliberately (ADR 0015). Flag it so it never gets auto-merged.

runsc (gVisor) updates are NOT applied by Flux — same host-substrate flow as k0s (ADR 0027 §6): the PR is a trigger, the containerd drop-in reload is a supervised action on the live node. Flag it so it never gets auto-merged.

cloudnative-pg/postgresql is NOT an independent dependency — it's a TOOL image (oidc-reconciler, restore-drill, chown init) that must mirror the CNPG database major (currently 17). The restore-drill boots a Postgres on data restored from the pg17 DB; pg18 binaries can't start a pg17 data dir, so a blind bump would break the backup drill. Renovate can't see the DB version (it's in a CNPG Cluster CRD it doesn't parse), so it must not drive this bump. The :17 tag already floats to the latest 17.x; bump every reference by hand, together, during a deliberate DB major migration.

Agora's images (server, harnesses, lab, showcase) are pinned by digest alone and moved by Agora's own CI: its propose-infra job keeps one rolling PR on the branch agora/images. Renovate cannot resolve a digest without a tag (dashboard lookup warnings) and must not race that PR.
Host tools installed by bootstrap.sh are not applied by Flux: merging the PR changes the pin, installing the binary on the node is a deliberate step.

RSSHub (apps/rss) has no releases, only an image per build, tagged with its date (2026-10-06). Renovate's docker versioning splits a tag at its first hyphen and would never see a newer one, so the date is the version here. Builds land several times a week: once a month is enough for a feed generator.
